Execute a 'Scopus' search plan, with optional caching and resume

Source: R/fetch_plan.R
scopus_fetch_plan.Rd

Runs every cell of a scopus_plan() in turn, optionally caching each cell's result so that an interrupted or quota-limited retrieval can resume without re-spending quota on the cells already fetched. Results are accumulated and bound once into a single scopus_records tibble.

Usage

scopus_fetch_plan(
  plan,
  max_results = Inf,
  cache_dir = NULL,
  resume = TRUE,
  api_key = NULL,
  inst_token = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE,
  cursor = FALSE,
  fields = c("core", "extended")
)

Arguments

plan

A scopus_plan object from scopus_plan().

max_results

Maximum records to retrieve per cell (default Inf). A finite cap is recorded on the result, and scopus_search_report() says which cells stopped at it.

cache_dir

Optional directory for per-cell cache files. The default of NULL performs no caching. Pass an explicit path you control, or scopus_cache_dir() to use a managed, clearable cache under tools::R_user_dir(). Caching happens only when you opt in through this argument. A cache directory serves one plan: cells are checkpointed by their position in the plan and their year, so give each distinct plan its own directory. As a safeguard, a checkpoint is served only when the query, year, view, page size and paging mode it was fetched under all match the plan cell, and only when its own max_results did not truncate it below what is being asked for now; anything else is a cache miss, refetched and overwritten. A checkpoint holding more records than the current max_results asks for is served trimmed to that cap, the fuller set staying on disk. A checkpoint that cannot be read back, for example one left half-written by an interrupted run, is also treated as a miss, and never aborts the harvest. A COMPLETE checkpoint written by a release that read authors from the first author alone (0.4.0 and earlier) is a miss as well, and is refetched once with a warning. STANDARD checkpoints from those releases are served as before, since their authors were read correctly. Checkpoints also record their fields. One fetched with fields = "extended" serves a core request, with the extra columns dropped, while a core one is a miss for an extended request and is refetched with a warning. A checkpoint written before the fields were recorded counts as core. A cache_dir that is not a directory and cannot be created as one, or in which no file can be created, is refused with a scopus_error_bad_input error before any request. A checkpoint that cannot be written all the same, for example on a full disk, gives a scopus_warning_cache_unwritable warning, and the cell's records are kept in the result.

resume

Logical. When TRUE and cache_dir is set, a cell whose cache file already exists is loaded from disk, sparing a second request.

api_key, inst_token

Optional credentials (see scopus_has_key()).

verbose

Logical. When TRUE, per-cell progress is reported.

cursor

Logical. When TRUE, each cell is retrieved with cursor-based pagination, which has no 5000-record ceiling, so a cell matching more records than that is retrieved whole and still checkpointed. The records then arrive in the API's deep-paging order (see scopus_fetch()). The default, FALSE, pages by offset, as plans always have, so a cell stops at its first 5000 records with a warning. Checkpoints record the paging mode and serve only requests made in the same mode. A checkpoint written before the mode was recorded counts as offset-paged. The Python twin's fetch_plan() pages by cursor unless told otherwise, the mode it has always used.

fields

"core" (the default) or "extended". "extended" also keeps the document type, source type, volume, issue, pages, ISSN, PubMed identifier and open-access status the Search API sends with every record, and the abstract under a COMPLETE plan. They arrive in the responses each cell already pays for, so they cost no extra quota. Like cursor, it is an argument of the fetch, since it changes how the records are read while the search returns the same records. See the Extended fields section of scopus_records().

Value

A scopus_records tibble combining all cells, with the originating plan attached as the plan attribute and the per-cell accounting as cell_totals, a tibble of cell, date, n_records and reported_total (the count the API gave for that cell, NA where it gave none). total_results is their sum, and is NA unless every cell reported one, since a partial sum would understate the search while looking like a real figure. A cell that comes back shorter than the API said it should warns, because a truncated or refused download otherwise arrives as a merely small result set; a cell stopped by max_results is short by request and does not warn. A finite max_results is attached as the attribute of that name, the cap of this call: a checkpoint written under a wider cap is served trimmed to it, so no cell holds more. scopus_search_report() reads all of this back. The retrieved_at, retrieved_until and scopusflow_version attributes described in scopus_fetch() are carried across from the cells. retrieved_at is the earliest of their times, since a combined set is only as fresh as its oldest cell. retrieved_until is the latest, the last search, which the record of a harvest resumed over several days has to give. Every version that contributed is listed, since resuming an older cache means more than one did. Each is omitted when any cell cannot supply it, as a checkpoint written before these attributes existed cannot. Dating the whole from the part of it that can be dated would misreport the set. A cell written before retrieved_until existed counts by its retrieved_at. paging and view are kept where every cell records the same one.

API access

Any cell not served from cache requires a valid API key and internet access. The API access section of scopus_count() gives the details.

See also

scopus_cache_dir(), scopus_cache_clear()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # scopusflow::scopus_has_key()
plan <- scopus_plan('"graphene supercapacitor"', years = 2015:2024,
                    field = "TITLE-ABS-KEY", partition = "year")
dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "graphene-cache")
# `max_results` caps each yearly cell, so the example stays small and
# quota-light; drop it to harvest every record in the plan.
recs <- scopus_fetch_plan(plan, max_results = 25, cache_dir = dir, resume = TRUE)
}
# The offline companion, which needs no key: a record set with a plan
# attached. 'Scopus' records may not be redistributed, so the bundled corpus
# of real articles stands in for the harvest. It came from OpenAlex's
# exact-phrase search for the same phrase, so the plan, one cell per year,
# describes a 'Scopus' search that was not run and would return other
# records.
plan <- scopus_plan('"graphene supercapacitor"', years = 2015:2024,
                    field = "TITLE-ABS-KEY", partition = "year")
recs <- example_records
attr(recs, "plan") <- plan
recs
